items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: The name 'Tim' appears only in the interviewer's stage direction '[INTERVIEWER] Tim, why don’t you flip that...'. There is no mention of a personal relationship between Helen Oakley Dance and Tim in the transcript.

ctx.x: Well it was all a pleasure. T-Bone was another personality like Chick. He was a wonderful person, and of course he was a wonderful guitarist, and a wonderful singer. And Stanley and I, Stanley had a friend who sent him records and we first heard him when we were there. And I’ve always loved blues anyways. And so I said to T-Bone in New York, I said, “I’m going to write a book about you.” He never heard of such a thing. And so his wife, who’s still alive and very nice and very sweet, and I said well I’ll come out…
Tim, why don’t you flip that, and then I’ll just wrap this up.
You know it was almost like a novel, and I knew the ending, but I wanted to say to T- Bone like don’t take that drink, you know, don’t— you wanted to — such a life, such a blues life.
